samples.summary: Typing strategy for the `.mjs` server modules changed (declaration files → `allowJs` + per-file `// @ts-check` + a `.mts` consumer test), but no design doc was added or updated. The canonical engine doc's §2 package layout still lists `src/server/stamp.d.mts` / `extract.d.mts` / `inject.d.mts` as the mechanism for typing the dynamic import, and the rationale for abandoning it (declaration file SHADOWS the implementation, so `@ts-check` never ran) survives only in a tsconfig comment (`packages/design-editor/tsconfig.json:27-44`) and a test-file docblock (`test/server/stamp.types.test.mts:5-22`). CONTRIBUTING.md:13-14,56-58 requires the existing doc under `docs/design/<area>/` be updated for a non-trivial change; this leaves the doc describing a shape the code deliberately rejects, and PRs 4+ (`inject.mjs`, `extract.mjs`) will follow the stale doc.
samples.evidence: engine doc §2 lists `inject.d.mts` / `extract.d.mts` / `stamp.d.mts`; the diff ships none and instead adds `allowJs` + `stamp.types.test.mts`, whose comment says it "replaces a `stamp.d.mts` that shipped with the prototype".

samples.summary: `data-wb-file` is silently dropped rather than escaped/refused when the path contains `"<>&`, and is also simply absent when `file` is undefined. Engine §7.9 states the attribute is what tells the host WHICH metadata tree to resolve a click against, and that "without the file the host must guess, and a wrong guess anchors the edit in the wrong file with no visible symptom". Degrading to no attribute therefore re-enables precisely the silent wrong-file anchoring the design says must not happen — the module's own header repeats this. Under the local-plugin pivot the plugin runs against arbitrary consumer trees, where `&` in a directory name is legal, so this is not a theoretical path. The design-consistent choices are to escape the value or to refuse to stamp the module, not to stamp it un-attributed; the test suite pins the degrade as intended behaviour.
samples.evidence: `const fileAttr = file && !/["<>&]/.test(file) ? ` data-wb-file="${file}"` : '';` — plus test 'is omitted rather than emitted broken…' asserting the node is still stamped without the file attribute.

samples.summary: `walkJsx(_sf, root, scope)` and `nodeAt(_sf, root, path)` carry an unused leading `SourceFile` parameter justified in-comment as "a published API whose argument positions three consumers already call by. Dropping it would be a breaking change to buy nothing." That justification does not hold in this tree: this is the file's first landing, no `extract.mjs`/`inject.mjs` exists yet, the only in-repo consumer (`stamp.mjs`) is written in this same PR, and the package is `private: true` and unpublished. The local-plugin doc's Risks section says these signatures become compatibility surface "the moment they hit npm" — i.e. this PR is the last cheap moment to drop the dead argument, not a moment when it is already frozen.
samples.evidence: jsx-nodes.mjs:522 `export function* walkJsx(_sf, root, scope = 'static')` and :734 `export function nodeAt(_sf, root, path)`; package.json has `"private": true` and no exports map.

samples.summary: `design-editor-local-plugin.md` §8 scopes PR 3 as "`jsx-nodes.mjs` + `extract.mjs` + `stamp.mjs`"; the diff lands only two of the three. With `extract.mjs` and `inject.mjs` absent, the module's central invariant ("THE JSX node model … three consumers that must agree byte-for-byte") has exactly one in-tree consumer, and the drift guard the tests advertise can only prove the stamper agrees. Not harmful on its own — a further split is legitimate — but flagging in case the extractor was meant to ride along.
samples.evidence: local-plugin doc §8 rollout table, row 3; diff adds src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs and src/server/stamp.mjs only.

verdict.reason: Absence verified. docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md:85-87 still lists `inject.d.mts` / `extract.d.mts` / `stamp.d.mts` as "Types for the dynamic import", while the tree contains no `.d.mts` at all and packages/design-editor/tsconfig.json:27-44 plus test/server/stamp.types.test.mts:17-22 explicitly reject that mechanism (a declaration file shadows the implementation so `// @ts-check` never ran). I grepped all of docs/ for allowJs, checkJs, @ts-check, .d.mts, pragma and declaration: no design doc (nor the pivot doc design-editor-local-plugin.md, nor the only design-editor task plan docs/tasks/active/20260729-design-editor-layout-sandbox-todo.md) records the new typing strategy; the string `allowJs` appears in no doc in the repo. So the reviewer's absence claim holds and the rationale survives only in a tsconfig comment and a test docblock. I record low confidence on the blocking judgement: CONTRIBUTING.md:55-59 scopes the mandatory design-doc update to "architecture / data-model changes" while lines 77-79 route refactors/chores straight to PR, and engine doc §2 is a prototype-branch snapshot (it lists vite.config.ts, main.tsx, scenes/, sandbox/ — none of which exist in this tree) whose header (lines 10-27) defers to the pivot doc, whose own target layout (local-plugin.md:113-129) lists `server/` with no declaration files. That is an interpretive argument for out-of-scope, not a counterexample, so it does not clear the refutation bar.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim at stamp.mjs:72 — `data-wb-file` is silently omitted (neither escaped nor refused) when the path contains `"<>&`, and when `file` is undefined, while the element is still stamped with `data-wb-node`/`data-wb-fp`. The behaviour is pinned by tests at stamp.test.mjs:215-219 and :221-230, which assert the node remains stamped without the file attribute. The design doc states the opposite intent: engine §7.9 (docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md:1174-1178) says the attribute tells the host which metadata tree to resolve against and that without it "a wrong guess anchors the edit in the wrong file with no visible symptom (checks 22, 24)", with check 22 at :1476-1478 being "Every stamp says which file it came from"; stamp.mjs's own header (:40-49, :62-64) repeats this and its inline comment (:69-71) claims it "refuses" when in fact only the attribute is dropped. No guard makes this unreachable: stampSource has no production caller in the tree (only stamp.mjs and the tests reference it), and design-editor-local-plugin.md:95,305 lists stamp.mjs as published, generic API that will run against foreign consumer trees where `&` in a path segment is legal. I could not name a refutation ground: the code is present as described, unguarded, and grounded in a written design invariant rather than mere taste, so it stays on the gate.
